headline: High: shared MCP and overlapping sensitive data create default leakage and injection pathways; TREK’s collaborative browser/network stack amplifies cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while TREK also exposes MCP and runs a browser. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one agent can be fed into the other as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is routed into TREK’s MCP or browser workflow without provenance tags
IF TREK ingests OpenBBTerminal-generated text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the agents for the session
Prefix all cross-agent content with a fixed data-only wrapper
Require manual review before TREK executes any OpenBBTerminal output
Log and reject any instruction-like tokens in transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. TREK also has allowlisted network egress and browser access, so if shared workspace or copied outputs exist, sensitive data can leave the pair. Because the interaction is undocumented, uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF either agent shares files, clipboard, or MCP payloads containing financial data, reservations, or secrets
IF TREK transmits copied OpenBBTerminal context to external services through its browser or allowlisted egress
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Block copy-paste of secrets and financial exports between agents
Disable browser access for TREK during cross-agent analysis
Redact API keys, MFA secrets, and account identifiers before transfer
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both use MCP, so they can contend over shared mutable resources if the operator points them at the same workspace or backend. OpenBBTerminal does not write the filesystem, but TREK has local files and collaborative state, making overlap plausible. The conflict is not guaranteed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared backend
IF TREK’s collaborative session and OpenBBTerminal’s API/MCP calls target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate MCP servers per agent
Avoid shared writable directories or databases
Serialize writes with an external lock
Run one agent at a time for any shared resource
requires-engineering: add resource-scoped locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and browser/network access, so it can plausibly act on OpenBBTerminal outputs. OpenBBTerminal produces financial-modeling outputs that TREK could render or use for planning without verification. That creates a default pathway from one agent’s facts into the other’s actions, with potentially irreversible downstream effects.
conditions: IF TREK consumes OpenBBTerminal outputs as authoritative travel or budget facts
IF TREK triggers bookings, edits, or user-visible recommendations from unverified OpenBBTerminal data
mitigations: Require a human verification step before TREK acts on OpenBBTerminal output
Mark OpenBBTerminal output as untrusted provenance
Compare critical facts against a second source before use
Disable auto-action flows from imported analysis
requires-engineering: add citation-aware validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, and secrets. TREK’s browser and allowlisted egress increase the chance that regulated or sensitive data crosses service boundaries. Because residency, retention, and certification details are undocumented for both, uncertainty warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF financial data, travel documents, or country visit history are shared across the pair
IF either agent stores or transmits that data under different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets
Review retention settings for both agents
Avoid sending travel documents or financial records through browser-backed flows
Document data residency for each service
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
